'''Ryloth''', also known as '''Twi'lek''', and '''Twi'lek Prime''',{{LivingForce|Oblivion's Kiss}} was the harsh, rocky [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]], an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] world located on the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] and forming one endpoint of the [[Death Wind Corridor/Legends|Death Wind Corridor]]. One side of the planet perpetually faced its [[Star/Legends|sun]] and the other remained in darkness, a phenomenon known as tidal locking. The dayside was referred to as the [[Bright Lands]] and the night-side was known as the [[Nightlands/Legends|Nightlands]]. ==Description== [[File:Nightlands.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The night side of Ryloth was punctuated by diverse, luminescent forests of crystalline flora]] Ryloth, the second [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Ryloth system/Legends|Ryloth system]], possessed a thin, but breathable [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The planet was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by five [[Moon/Legends|moons]], which had subtle tidal effects on the planet's liquid core and underground springs. It had little or no surface [[Water/Legends|water]] except for patches of water ice on the night side. It was a planet of extremes: dry, rocky landscapes of deserts, mountain ranges with mist-covered peaks, shadowy valleys, alternated with snowy wastes, joined by lush temperate bands which concentrated much of its population. Because of its unusual day-night rotation period, atmospheric conditions on Ryloth's surface were characterized by turbulent seasons and extremely high winds (reaching 500 kilometers per hour) scouring the surface and sculpting the landscape and unpredictable bursts of heat called [[heat storm]]s, which could reach 300 degrees Celsius. The more extreme heat storms sometimes moved across the terminator and reached miles underground, making caves near the surface temporarily uninhabitable, before eventually dying out on the night side. Along the terminator lay a thin habitable border, a twilight realm between the two extremes. Along this narrow strip were the series of caverns where some of the Twi'leks decided to build their underground cities, blockaded with thick blast doors and portcullises to keep out the vicious monsters that prowled the Bright Lands, especially [[Lylek/Legends|lyleks]]. The [[Floating Rock Gardens of Ryloth]] were a natural wonder and tourist attraction, well known throughout the Outer Rim, where strong winds blew among the tunnels, causing rocks to float gently through the air. Over the years the gardens became filled with rare and dazzling stones. Visitors were allowed to rearrange the stones to their liking, but were encouraged to seek meaning in the natural configurations. [[Kala'uun/Legends|Kala'uun]] was a permanent city located within the [[Lonely Five Range|Lonely Five mountain range]], boasting a large underground [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. It was the center of interplanetary commerce on Ryloth, and as such contained the large businesses [[Galactic Exotics]] and [[Schaum/Yfarg/Welbig/Fabrico and Associates|SchaumAssociates]], as well as the outer rim offices of [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]. To people like [[Jerris Rudd]] and others who have been to Ryloth and [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], they describe the planet being a little bit like Tatooine.{{StoryCite|story=A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}} ===Fauna===
[[File:Gutkurr_pair.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A pair of [[Gutkurr/Legends|gutkurrs]]]]
Ryloth had several native [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] species, most of which were fierce and predatory for survival on a planet with such a harsh environment. The [[Lylek/Legends|lylek]] was easily the most dangerous predator native to Ryloth, with their hard shelled [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] bodies and sharp limbs and extremely strong tentacles. They were one of only a few creatures able to withstand the extreme temperatures of the [[Bright Lands]]. The [[Doashim/Legends|doashim]] was another fierce predator that inhabited the dark subterranean caverns of Ryloth. They were horned, red-eyed, sharp-clawed and fanged creatures reminiscent of demons from the lore of many different sentient species across the galaxy. The [[Gutkurr/Legends|gutkurr]] were fast, two-legged creatures with hard-shelled carapaces with spines protruding from their backs. They were predatory creatures feared by the Twi'leks. One of the few non-aggressive creatures of Ryloth was the [[Rycrit/Legends|rycrit]], which were short-furred quadrupeds kept as herd animals by the Twi'leks. They were raised for their hides, which could be used for clothing, and for their meat which was often used in [[rycrit stew]]. ==History== [[File:Twilek_Exodus.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Twi'leks flee a [[heat storm]].]] Ryloth was originally discovered by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] explorers approximately 10,000 years before the onset of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and was one of the first worlds discovered in the Outer Rim. Located at one end of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]], it was one of the few worlds of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] further from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Galactic Core]] than Tatooine. Civilization on Ryloth at the time of its discovery was not particularly advanced. Twi'leks integrated windmills and turbines to power their homes and industries carved out of the mountains. The cultivation of fungi and molds provided nourishment for the populace, as did the rearing of the domesticated herd animals [[Rycrit/Legends|rycrits]] for meat. Twi'leks never developed [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel, but instead expanded throughout the galaxy by trading with the Republic, variously negotiating, charming, or seducing their way to the stars. ===Life of enslavement=== The [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] trade had been an everyday part of life on Ryloth for millennia and persisted long after its contact with the Republic sometime in [[10,000 BBY]]. Dancing girls were especially prized, and as Twi'lek communities were established throughout the Republic and elsewhere, they found numerous eager markets. The slaves were often sold by 'contract,' as a feeble way of evading antislavery laws.
[[File:Twilek_twins.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Twi'lek slave girls]]
Female Twi'lek consorts and companions soon became a status symbol among the rich and the decadent throughout the Galactic Republic and eventually the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The slave trade remained profitable all throughout Ryloth's history, and though the early slavers were Twi'leks, over the years many alien [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] migrated to Ryloth for a piece of the action. Twi'leks of all professions eventually became a common, even ubiquitous, sight all over the galaxy, as businesspeople, servants, bodyguards, [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomos]] and slaves. Their near-[[Human/Legends|Human]] appearance made them less a target of anti-[[Alien/Legends|alien]] prejudice than others during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial era]]. The [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] crime lord [[Graxol Kelvyyn/Legends|Graxol Kelvyyn]] had his headquarters on Ryloth shortly before the onset of the Clone Wars. He was known for having a vast slave-trading network that covered the Outer Rim and even reached [[Kidiet Olgo]] in the Galactic Core. Prominent examples of Twi'lek slaves during the last days of the Republic and the Empire included [[Ann Gella/Legends|Ann Gella]] and [[Tann Gella/Legends|Tann Gella]], twins owned by [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], and [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], owned by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. ===Ryll=== The major export of Ryloth, and the product which sustained its early trade, was the mineral known as [[Ryll/Legends|ryll]], a potent [[Spice/Legends|spice]], discovered in [[4800 BBY]], which was [[Mining/Legends|mined]] and originally distributed for medicinal use. Ryll was found in 'blooms' in the rock rather than veins, typical of most ores. Miners placed their mines underneath the blooms and drilled up. Ryll's highly addictive nature and hallucinogenic properties also made it a favorite recreational substance among the scoundrels and decadent nobles of the galaxy. A particularly popular and addictive mixture was [[glitteryll]], a synthetic mixture of ryll and [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]] which had a strong numbing effect on memory. Ryll and glitteryll were outlawed on most Republic worlds, but the demand was great enough to sustain a healthy [[Black market/Legends|black market]]. Crime lords and slavers turned their attention to ryll [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] operations and began competing with legitimate miners. By the time of the [[Jedi Civil War]], most ''legitimate'' ryll mining operations were gone, leaving only the smugglers. The exclusive distribution rights to ryll were temporarily seized by the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] around 4800 BBY. Though it was thought this might end the perilous illegal ryll trade, it had quite the opposite effect. Irresponsible distribution of the drug eventually led to the [[Gank Massacres]]. ===Jedi Knights on Ryloth=== [[File:Heatstorm-Redemption1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Tott Doneeta]] leading fellow Twi'leks away from a heat storm on Ryloth in [[3986 BBY]]]] At one point, the [[Gugal bloom]] decimated the [[Forest/Legends|forests]] of Ryloth. Around [[1002 BBY]], the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] operated a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] academy on the world that specialized in the training of [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassins]].''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'' In the years before the Clone Wars, [[Anoon Bondara]] served as [[Jedi Watchman/Legends|Jedi Watchman]] of Ryloth, identifying Force-sensitive Twi'leks and sending them to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for training. In [[46 BBY/Legends|46 BBY]],{{JCFCite|url=posts/13327474|board=Literature|thread=The Official Jan Duursema Discussion Thread|user=Jan_Duursema|date=2003-09-25|time=10:08 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625181621/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-official-jan-duursema-discussion-thread.5915607/page-36|quote=Aayla was 2 when Quin and Tholme found her on Ryloth. Quin was 11. So there's 9 years difference in age. Quin is Obi-Wan's age--which I think was stated as 25 during Ep I. So Aayla would be 16 at the time of Ep I.}} {{C|Note: In response to a question directed to Jan Duursema by [[Billy Buehler]] (aka The2ndQuest) on the [[Jedi Council Forums]], Jan Duursema explained that Aayla "would have been about 10" & "Quin about 19" during the flashback sequence in ''[[Jedi: Aayla Secura]]'' depicting Quinlan Vos taking Aayla as his Padawan.}} [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] and [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] were sent to Ryloth under orders to stop illegal animal smuggling. There they met a Force-sensitive infant Twi'lek named [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]]. She was taken and later trained by Quinlan Vos.''[[Jedi: Aayla Secura]]'' Later in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Vos and Aayla, now his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], discovered an illegal glitteryll smuggling operation masterminded by Aayla's uncle [[Pol Secura]], [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]], and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Chom Frey Kaa]], using [[energy spider]] eggs taken from [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]]. Using the mental abilities of the [[Kiffar/Legends|Kiffar]] [[Asanté Vos]] and large doses of glitteryl, Pol Secura wiped their memories and kept Aayla as a dancer in his estate. Eventually, Vos recovered his memories and returned to Ryloth to retrieve his Padawan.''[[Star Wars: Twilight]]'' ===Ryloth in the Republic=== Ryloth entered into the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] circa [[10,000 BBY]]. Ryloth was represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by Senators [[Connus Trell]] and [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], who succeeded the controversial [[Chom Frey Kaa]]. Senator Free Taa, a strong [[Loyalist/Legends|Loyalist]], kept Ryloth under the Republic's protection by supporting most of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] decrees, including the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]].
[[File:Blockade_of_Ryloth.png|thumb|left|200px|Ryloth [[Ryloth blockade/Legends|blockaded]] by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]] forces]]
===Clone Wars=== During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Ryloth was invaded by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and was used to house a large [[Droid/Legends|droid]] reclamation facility under the eye of [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]]. At first the Republic Garrison, under the command of [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Ima-Gun Di/Legends|Ima-Gun Di]] and [[Clone Captain/Legends|Clone Capt]]. [[Keeli/Legends|Keeli]] fought the droids alongside [[Twi'lek freedom fighters/Legends|Twi'lek freedom fighters]] under Gen. [[Cham Syndulla/Legends|Cham Syndulla]] to protect the refugees. Unfortunately, supplies were running low and the droid army was closing in on their position. When a Republic fleet under Admiral [[Dao/Legends|Dao]] failed to make it past the [[Ryloth blockade/Legends|Ryloth blockade]], Gen. Di decided to sacrifice himself and his command to buy the Twi'leks time to escape. Though Gen. Di and his command perished, supplies sent from [[Toydaria/Legends|Toydaria]] reached the refugees.{{TCW|Supply Lines}} After the droids took control of Ryloth, the Twi'leks were taken captive and some were used as human shields for the droid army. The seizure was officially protested by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], and public opinion on Ryloth itself was bitterly divided. The [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|battle]] was short, but Ryloth's towns were left heavily damaged by [[Hyena-class bomber/Legends|droid bombers]]. Eventually, the planet became the site of a battle in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] during the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]]. ===Galactic Empire=== [[File:BattleOfRyloth-EaW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Battle of Ryloth (Galactic Civil War)|The Battle of Ryloth]]]] The anti-alien prejudice of the Galactic Empire was clear to the inhabitants of Ryloth. [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]] thought little of aliens, but Ryloth shrewdly played the role of loyal servant to the Empire, while quietly and unobtrusively aiding the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. These were dark times for the Twi'leks, however, as even members of the most influential clans were enslaved, losing all their property and influence to entertain and see to the needs of Imperial bureaucrats and [[Governor/Legends|governors]]. For a time, roughly the same year as the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Rebellion operated a base on Ryloth. It was located by [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]], prompting an attack by an Imperial task force, which infiltrated and wiped out the installation, despite strong resistance from the Rebels and even from immigrant [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]]. During this time, the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] owned a secret [[Consortium palace]] on Ryloth. In [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] established a refueling outpost on Ryloth, using Twi'lek slave labor, and recruited native Twi'lek [[Tol Sivron]] to administer the outpost now called [[Maw Installation]].''[[Champions of the Force]]'' In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], [[Tyneir Renz]], [[Padija Anjeri]], [[Nikaede Celso]], and [[Drake Paulsen]] brought the crystal skull of Twi'lek [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Newar Forrth]] to the Rebel base on [[Derora]]. Renz presented the skull to the [[Nercathi clan]] on Ryloth to persuade them to join the Alliance.{{JournalCite|12|Idol Intentions}}{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050526a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 4: Of the Crudest Matter}} ===After the Empire=== [[File:KalauunStarport-PlattsStarportGuide.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Kala'uun Starport]] on Ryloth]] Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Ryloth became a member of the [[Alliance of Free Planets]]. However, after it was liberated from the Empire, Ryloth chose not to join the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] right away. Later, [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and [[Winter Celchu|Winter]] would journey to Ryloth in search of a fugitive Twi'lek, and had to compete with a group of Imperials in a rigged race.''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Battleground: Tatooine]]'' After [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] went to Ryloth in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]] to get ryll to help heal the [[Krytos virus]], Twi'lek pilots joined Wedge Antilles and former pilots of Rogue Squadron in fighting [[Ysanne Isard]] in the [[Bacta War]]. Due to their [[ryll kor]] scams against the New Republic, the [[Clan Shak|Shak clan]] was discredited.''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]'' Shortly after that, the Twi'lek [[Nolaa Tarkona]] engineered a revolution that overthrew the ruling clans. She then assumed control of Ryloth and founded the [[Anti-Humanism|anti-Human]] [[Diversity Alliance]]. However, in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], the Diversity Alliance's efforts to launch a war against Humans was foiled. Following that, the planet was represented in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] by [[Kur (Twi'lek)|Kur]]''[[Young Jedi Knights: The Emperor's Plague]]'' and later by [[Cola Quis]].''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]'' During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the planet was a valuable member of the New Republic and the subsequent [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. During the [[Second Imperial Civil War]] it was part of the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]]. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Ryloth_TEA.jpg|thumb|180px|Ryloth in ''The Essential Atlas'']] The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Ryloth in the [[Orus sector/Legends|Orus sector]], which is actually a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]. Additionally, ''Rebellion''{{'s}} in-game encyclopedia entry for Ryloth erroneously states that most of the planet's inhabitants live in perpetual darkness on the side of the world that eternally faces away from its sun. Despite Ryloth's lack of rotation in earlier portrayals, the Ryloth story arc in the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' instead shows day and night on the planet, as well as a mention of its "planetary rotation." This was later confirmed as a [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] rather than an error in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', although the planet was still mentioned to have harsh environmental conditions. The Twi'lek cities built within caverns have been compared to real-life locations such as the [[Wikipedia:Ancient Pueblo Peoples|Anasazi]] people ruins of [[Wikipedia:Mesa Verde National Park|Mesa Verde National Park]] in south-western [[Wikipedia:Colorado|Colorado]], which were discovered by two cowboys in 1887.[[Star Wars Kids (1997) 20|''Star Wars Kids'' (1997) 20]] ==Appearances==
